title: Chewy Amaretti
summary: Chewy almond biscuits with a cracked, sugar-dusted crust, rested before baking so the tops split open in the oven.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix the almonds
steps.text: Mix the ground almonds, caster sugar, salt and lemon zest together in a bowl. Combining the dry ingredients first means the egg white will fold through evenly in the next step.

steps.title: Whisk whites and fold in
steps.text: Whisk the egg whites to soft, foamy peaks that just hold their shape at the tips, then fold them into the almond mixture with the almond flavouring to form a thick, sticky paste. Only lightly whisking the whites keeps the paste dense enough to shape into balls rather than collapsing.

steps.title: Shape and coat
steps.text: With damp hands, roll the mixture into 20g balls, then roll each generously in icing sugar. Space them 4cm apart on the lined trays; damp hands stop the sticky paste clinging to your fingers.

steps.title: Rest to form a skin
steps.text: Leave the balls uncovered at room temperature for 1 hour, so a dry skin forms on the outside. This skin is what cracks open during baking to give amaretti their characteristic crackled top.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: During the resting time, heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) for at least 20 minutes. A moderate, fully heated oven bakes the amaretti through without drying out their chewy centres.

steps.title: Bake until cracked
steps.text: Bake for 20-24 minutes, until the tops are cracked and light golden at the base, and the biscuits feel just firm on the outside but still soft when pressed. That softness under a firm crust is exactly what keeps them chewy once cooled.

steps.title: Cool and firm up
steps.text: Cool on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. They firm up slightly as they cool but stay soft and chewy in the middle.

tips: Don't skip the hour-long rest - baking straight away, before a skin has formed, is the main reason amaretti stay smooth instead of cracking open as they bake.
Keep your hands damp while shaping, as dry hands make the sticky paste impossible to roll neatly.
Whisk the egg whites only to soft peaks; stiffer whites are harder to fold evenly into the heavy almond paste and leave streaks.
Roll the balls generously in icing sugar so the coating is thick enough to crackle attractively as the biscuit expands.
Take them out while the centres still feel soft to the touch - they firm up on cooling, so they'll turn hard if left in the oven until they feel fully set.
storage: Store in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 1 week. They can be frozen for up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature before serving.
